name: Topaz-Furnace
description: Topaz-Furnace burns with a golden fury, its surface a cracked mosaic of cooling magma plates separated by rivers of molten rock that glow amber and white. Three supervolcanoes dominate the northern hemisphere, their eruption plumes reaching the upper atmosphere and raining glassy topaz-colored tephra across thousands of kilometers. Where the planetary core breaches the surface, the light is so intense that unfiltered observation causes immediate retinal damage.

The toxic atmosphere reeks of sulfur dioxide and particulate ash, coating every surface in fine golden dust. The heat is relentless, pressing through even the best thermal shielding like a living weight. At night, if it can be called that, the magma flows provide their own illumination, painting the smog-heavy sky in shades of copper and flame.

A corporate mining consortium operated here for eleven years before a caldera collapse buried their primary facility under two kilometers of fresh basalt. The surface installations remain partially intact, their heat-resistant structures testament to extraordinary engineering. Microbial life thrives in the geothermal vents, extremophiles whose biochemistry has yielded insights into heat-resistant metallurgy.

The platinum deposits alone justify the risk of return, and salvage crews periodically brave the surface to strip what remains of the mining complex. Each visit is a race against seismic instability, and the planet has claimed more than a dozen ships that lingered too long. Topaz-Furnace does not forgive hesitation.
